newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's '96 cement import seen at 2 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's '96 cement import seen at 2 mln tonnes.

text.p: Malaysia's total cement imports in 1996 will reach an estimated two million tonnes, cement manufacturer Kedah Cement Holdings Bhd said on Thursday.
"This should stabilise the current shortage of cement the country is facing at the moment," Lim Yen Haat, joint managing director of KCHB, told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
Lim said he expected total demand for cement to reach 14 million tonnes this year.
"The majority of imports are being sourced from the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) region," he said. "But imports have also been coming in from as far away as Mexico."
Lim Yan Hai, group deputy chairman said KCHB had no immediate plans to expand capacity further.
KCHB, the country's largest cement manufacturer, has an installed production capacity of 3.3 million tonnes per year.
The company has benefited from Malaysia's current construction boom, with demand growing at around 13 percent in 1996, according to a report by Jupiter Securities in July.
